subject: Unexpected prefetch burst on Apr 30 — invoice and VAT triage
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir@opslytics.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: billing@opslytics.com
Date: Tue, 09 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Invoice question: unexpected prefetch burst on April 30 (VAT?)

Hi Hannah,

We just pulled April invoices and saw a large overage line attributed to a prefetch burst on 2028-04-30 (~1.3M prefetch tokens). I attached our internal export (opslytics_usage_q1.csv) showing the spike. The charge pushed us over the committed tier by ~18k USD which is material for our month.

Can you help clarify what caused the burst? Two specific asks:
- Is this something on our side (we're checking staging jobs) or a server-side duplication?
- For VAT treatment: we are EU-registered (billing@opslytics.com handles VAT) — if you issue a credit, does that change VAT liability or do we need to provide a VAT ID to apply reverse charge?

We can share a short session id and request ids if that helps. Appreciate quick help — billing cutover is next week.

Best,
Samir Khan
Head of Platform
Opslytics

Attachment: opslytics_usage_q1.csv (CSV, 72KB)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir@opslytics.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 09 May 2028 12:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Invoice question: unexpected prefetch burst on April 30 (VAT?)

Thanks for the heads up, Samir — sorry for the surprise. I'm looping in Ben from Billing Ops and Kimberly from Revenue Tax so we can triage and give a clear remediation path.

Ben/Kim: can you pull the usage traces for Opslytics for 2028-04-30 and confirm whether the high prefetch count was caused by double-sends or a client-side staging job? If it's on our side, we'll propose a provisional credit and withhold collection while we investigate. If it's on the customer side, we'll detail the breakdown and suggest next steps for avoiding recurrence.

Samir: we'll aim to get a preliminary root-cause and an interim credit proposal within 48 hours. If you can forward a sample request id or the time window from your CSV (start/end timestamps), that will speed verification.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Revenue Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0123

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: Samir Khan <samir@opslytics.com>
Date: Wed, 10 May 2028 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Invoice question: unexpected prefetch burst on April 30 (VAT?)

Quick update from Billing Ops after a first pass on telemetry:
- We correlated Opslytics customer-id (cust_OpSly_021) to a surge of prefetch requests between 2028-04-30T02:10:00Z and 2028-04-30T02:28:00Z.
- Sampling of request ids shows identical prompt hashes repeated ~3x in short succession; traces indicate a client retry loop combined with a misconfigured SDK that re-issued prefetches when it didn't get a quick ACK.
- No server-side duplication pattern (no known replay job or pipeline retry on Redwood side).

Attached is the invoice in question for reference (invoice_2028-04-30.pdf).

Proposed interim steps:
1) Offer a provisional credit for the incremental overage amount up to $18,200 USD while Opslytics validates staging job logs.
2) Hold collection on that invoice until we have confirmation (30-day hold).
3) Post-validate: if Opslytics confirms staging misconfig, treat as customer-side; if we find a platform issue in deeper logs, we will issue full refund + process VAT reversal where applicable.

Kimberly — can you advise whether a provisional credit requires any VAT handling on our invoice (reverse charge vs gross credit) for an EU entity pending their VAT ID? I've included the HubSpot ticket and telemetry link for traceability: https://hubspot.com/deal/OPSLY-3921 and https://console.redwood.ai/telemetry/opslytics/prefetch/2028-04-30

Ben Carter
Billing Operations Lead | Redwood Inference
Attachment: invoice_2028-04-30.pdf (PDF, 48KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir@opslytics.com>, ben_carter@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 14:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Invoice question: unexpected prefetch burst on April 30 (VAT?)

Thanks everyone — quick tax note and proposed customer-facing language.

Tax guidance: for EU B2B customers we can apply the reverse-charge mechanism if Opslytics provides a valid VAT ID that matches billing details. If they cannot provide a VAT ID, Redwood must issue a gross credit (VAT-inclusive) and adjust our VAT remittance accordingly.

Proposed resolution steps to send Opslytics (please review):
- Redwood will place invoice 2028-04-30 on a 30-day collection hold immediately.
- We will provisionally apply a credit of USD 18,200 against the invoice while customer and Redwood Ops complete log validation. This is labeled as a provisional adjustment and subject to final reconciliation.
- If Opslytics provides their EU VAT ID within 14 days and validation confirms platform-side overcharge, Redwood will reissue the credit with reverse-charge annotation and provide a corrected invoice/credit note. If Opslytics cannot provide VAT ID and we determine the credit is warranted, Redwood will issue a VAT-inclusive credit note and process the VAT amendment.

Samir — can you confirm the billing entity's VAT ID and accept the provisional credit hold so we can pause collection? Suggested short message for Opslytics: "We’ve placed your April 30 invoice on hold and applied a provisional credit of USD 18,200 while we jointly verify the usage spike. Please provide your EU VAT ID if available so we can finalize VAT treatment."

Hannah/Ben: if you approve, I’ll instruct Finance to create the provisional credit memo and tag the HubSpot deal OPSLY-3921 with the hold. Vanessa — please coordinate the communications and update the invoice status.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Revenue Accountant | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0166
